lines.say: Why does the scale jump after a cheat meal?
Why does this happen, number eighteen.
You eat a big meal, wake up, and you're two kilos heavier. That's not two kilos of fat.
Carbs get stored in your muscles and liver as glycogen. Each gram of glycogen holds about three grams of water.
Salty food makes your body hold even more water. And the food itself is still in your gut.
To gain one kilo of fat, you'd need to eat about seven and a half thousand extra calories. Most meals don't come close.
So don't panic. The water drops in a few days if you eat normally again.
Watch your weekly average, not one morning.
